title: Kilwa Kisiwani
summary: Kilwa Kisiwani, on an island off Tanzania's coast, was a Swahili trading city occupied from the 9th to the 19th century and most prosperous in the 13th and 14th. Its merchants traded gold and ivory from the interior for goods from Arabia, India and China. Ibn Battuta visited in 1331-1332. Coral-stone ruins include the Great Mosque, built in the 11th century, and the Husuni Kubwa palace of about 1310-1333. The Portuguese attacked in 1505.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says the island was occupied from the 9th to the 19th century with peak prosperity in the 13th and 14th, and trade prominence from the 13th to the 16th; World History Encyclopedia dates the Portuguese attack to 1505. The span is the 13th-16th centuries.
